description: Intent i009 (SNAPSHOT=s02, BRANCH=l2-wireless-ie-tlv) complete. Findings in s02: (1) net/wireless/scan.c:307 cfg80211_gen_new_ie first loop — condition "while (tmp_old + tmp_old[1] + 2 - ie <= ielen)" dereferences the attacker-controlled IE length byte tmp_old[1] with no remaining>=2 check; when the cursor lands on the final lone byte (offset ielen-1, reachable via attacker-chosen length advances) it reads one byte past the remote beacon/probe IE buffer, exactly the seed mechanism (id consumed, size read at remaining==1); source is remote MBSSID beacon data via cfg80211_inform_bss_data->cfg80211_parse_mbssid_data->cfg80211_gen_new_ie. (2) scan.c:367 second loop of the same function — "while (tmp_new + tmp_new[1] + 2 - sub_copy <= subie_len)" reads sub_copy[subie_len] past the kmemdup'd attacker-controlled merged MBSSID profile (heap 1-byte OOB, KASAN-detectable) and uses it to drive memcpy/advance. (3) net/wireless/util.c:1576 skip_ie reads "u8 len = ies[pos + 1]" (and again at 1585) without confirming pos+1<ielen; it is reached from ieee80211_ie_split/ric (util.c:1612/1627/1632) whose callers pass nl80211-supplied assoc_data->ie / extra_ies that may end with a lone element-ID byte — medium confidence because the source is a CAP_NET_ADMIN local user, not remote. Safe candidates verified with exact guards: cfg80211_is_element_inherited (scan.c:244 datalen<3+id_len checks), cfg80211_get_p2p_attr (util.c:1461 len<2 and iedatalen+2>len checks, the canonical fixed shape), for_each_element macro (include/linux/ieee80211.h:3783 requires header+body in-bounds), cfg80211_parse_mbssid_data walk (scan.c:2087). Bounded negative evidence: all examined 802.11 IE walkers except the two cfg80211_gen_new_ie loops and skip_ie enforce a remaining>=2 or full header+body bound before reading the length byte. Limitations: Bluetooth EIR/AD/SDP/AMP and radiotap parsers in s02 were not searched before early finalization; net/mac80211/util.c:2749 walk and he.c/ht.c element readers were located but bodies unread; no runtime reproducer was built (source-level analysis of a read-only tree), and exploit impact beyond the 1-byte OOB read is unproven.
